directions.name: Multi-yaw generate-and-SELECT (min-local-gradient) for the near-ground seam
directions.summary: Survives as the single strongest NEW T1 lever, but with TIGHTENED, decisive kill gating because the whole bet rides on one unverified assumption: that yaw rotation actually DECORRELATES the near-ground seam artifact. It exploits two real assets -- the LoRA's trained yaw-equivariance (progress.md line 15 lists yaw-loss as a training objective) and the project's own CONFIRMED single-source>averaging finding (MEMORY: ghost=averaging, single-source FIXED it) -- via SELECT-not-average, which by construction cannot introduce a net-new object beyond what one gate-passing pass already contains. progress.md line 11(e) pre-registers 'yaw-SELECT' as an optional next step, so it is sanctioned, not speculative. The mechanism is sound IF the artifact decorrelates; the pilot settles that for ~1.5 hr.
directions.how_to_test: init=bevfinal. Use external/DiT360/src/yaw_rotate.equirectangular_rotate_yaw VERBATIM (verified: for a full 1024x2048 ERP, orig_H=W//2=1024==crop_H so start_row=0, full phi span, theta wrap via atan2 -> a geometrically exact full-pano yaw; padding_mode='border' is irrelevant at start_row=0). directions.gpu_cost_est: Pilot 3 offsets ~1.5 A100-hr (3 inverts, since the image changes per yaw, + 3 reverse). Full 8 offsets ~4 A100-hr only if pilot passes. SELECT/rotate is CPU-seconds.
directions.kill_criteria: KILL at the 3-offset pilot, BEFORE any 8-offset spend, if EITHER: (a) the seam-band cross-offset variance is near-zero (same wave at the same registered location every pass) -> yaw does not decorrelate this rig-geometry artifact, abandon; OR (b) min-gradient SELECT yields a blocky/patchwork seam (the dead DiT-oracle loose-select failure mode, progress.md). Also KILL if any single yaw pass at r008/tau5 already trips the gate (would mean even the thin cell hallucinates under rotation). The variance map is the decisive 1-screenshot test.
directions.expected_payoff: Medium. If the wave decorrelates it is the only lever that can collapse a defect single-pass cannot, and it rides a confirmed project win-pattern. If it does not decorrelate, the pilot kills it for 1.5 hr with no wasted 8-offset run.

directions.name: RF editing-window shrink (stop_timestep sweep) for thin seam-hide
directions.summary: The single highest-leverage unswept knob. Our runner pins start_timestep=0.0/stop_timestep=0.99 so eta=1 anchors the WHOLE loop while the seam core free-runs all the way to t=0 — exactly the late-step free-running that the done-list proved invents cars (D2, v3). Shrink the editing window so the model only nudges seam structure in EARLY high-noise steps then snaps back to the source trajectory. This re-textures the wavy seam without the late-step object invention, attacking the no-op-vs-melt dichotomy from the un-tried 'window' axis rather than the already-dead mask-size/tau axis.
directions.how_to_test: init=SR_bmw_bevfinal_1024x2048.png; mask=SR_bmw_seamcore.png thin r008 core (h016 halo), exactly the v14 trimap that the user liked. Add two args to run_dit360_trimap_clamp.py main (currently hardcoded at line 384-385): plumb --start-timestep (fixed 0.0) and --stop-timestep into the pipe() call. Sweep stop_timestep in {0.20, 0.35, 0.50, 0.99(=current control)}. 4 cases, single FLUX load, single invert (window is reverse-only). For each: torchvision object gate (netnew=0 required) + vision on _raw.png, and report core/halo/far MAE vs init. WIN = MAE in core rises above the v14-tau5 no-op floor (~30) AND gate clean AND vision shows smoother seam.
directions.gpu_cost_est: ~1 A100-hour: 1 load (~60s) + 1 invert (~90s) + 4 reverse passes (~3min each). Cheapest possible non-trivial experiment.
directions.kill_criteria: If even stop_timestep=0.20 either (a) under-changes (core MAE still ~= tau5 no-op floor, raw ~= hard_select) OR (b) trips the object gate on any setting, then the window knob does not break the seam dichotomy -> CLOSE T1-DiT as cosmetic-only (consistent with done-list prior).

directions.novelty_note: Done-list swept tau MAGNITUDE, mask SIZE, steps, seed, guidance, and all POST-COMPOSE operators — but NEVER start/stop_timestep (runner hardcodes 0.0/0.99). The done-list 'invents cars' results were all at the FULL 0.99 window; shrinking the window is a distinct, untested mechanism, not a re-run of v3/v9/D2.

directions.name: Multi-yaw generate-and-SELECT (not average) for seam-hide
directions.summary: Weaponizes the LoRA's trained yaw-equivariance PLUS the project's own confirmed single-source>averaging finding. Run the SAME thin-seam edit at N spherical yaw offsets; each pass lands the residual near-ground wave at a different azimuth/phase. Rotate each result back and SELECT per-region the lowest-local-gradient pixels along the seam band (NEVER average). Because every candidate pixel is a real DiT render of source-anchored content (no new mask region), and selection only picks the cleanest existing pixel, no net-new object can be introduced beyond what a single pass already passes the gate on.
directions.how_to_test: init=SR_bmw_bevfinal_1024x2048.png. Use external/DiT360/src/yaw_rotate.equirectangular_rotate_yaw verbatim. PILOT first with 3 offsets {0,120,240} deg: for each offset o, yaw-rotate init by +o, also yaw-rotate the seamcore mask by +o (so the seam strip tracks), run the winning thin-seam config from Direction 1 (or v14 r008/tau8), yaw-rotate the _raw output by -o to re-register. Stack 3 re-registered panos; SELECT per-pixel argmin of local Sobel gradient energy in a band around the seam, copy source elsewhere. Gate+vision the selected pano. If artifacts decorrelate (the 3 passes differ in the seam band), expand to 8 offsets {0,45,...,315}.
directions.gpu_cost_est: Pilot 3 offsets ~1.5 A100-hr (3 inverts + 3 reverse; invert must redo per yaw since image changes). Full 8 offsets ~4 A100-hr. SELECT/rotate is CPU-cheap.
directions.kill_criteria: If the 3-offset pilot shows the seam-band artifact does NOT decorrelate across offsets (same wave at same registered location every pass) -> abandon before 8. If min-gradient selection produces a patchwork/blocky seam (like the dead DiT-oracle loose-select) -> kill.
directions.expected_payoff: Medium. Strongest NEW lever the panorama-prior lens surfaced; directly exploits an existing project win-pattern (single-source select). If it works it collapses the wave that single-pass cannot.
directions.novelty_note: Done-list multi-SEED (v9) is replacing the noise seed at fixed geometry and was a closed loophole; multi-YAW is a SPHERICAL re-projection that decorrelates artifacts by AZIMUTH (a different mechanism, exploiting the trained yaw-loss). SELECT-not-average is explicitly aligned with the project's confirmed finding and was never run for DiT outputs (DiT-oracle selected from source pixels, not from a yaw-ensemble of DiT renders).

directions.name: Real-evidence donor reference (shift_mask / swapped batch[0]) to bound seam fill
directions.summary: Converts DiT360 from a self-consistency clamp into a real-evidence rein. The attn processor already supports reading reference tokens from batch[0] at `mask` and WRITING them into batch[1] at an independent `shift_mask` (utils.shift_tensor exists), and pipe.invert() accepts ANY donor image. Today both are self-reference. Point the donor at the CLEAN neighbor-cam pixels of the same physical surface (or an alternative clean stitch e.g. virtual-centre single-source). The seam then gets repainted from real adjacent-camera appearance that actually exists, not from FLUX's text/self prior — bounding hallucination to real evidence, which is precisely why it stays gate-clean.
directions.how_to_test: init/canvas=bevfinal as batch[1]. Donor (batch[0]) = the existing virtual-centre single-source stitch SR (already a project deliverable) OR a per-seam neighbor-cam ERP slab. Two sub-tests: (A) cheap shift_mask: pass shift_mask (donor strip a few latent cols across the seam, target=wavy strip) into PersonalizeAnythingAttnProcessor via the runner's lambda; keep tau low (10-15) so token-replace dominates early. (B) swapped-donor invert: call pipe.invert(image=donor_stitch) for batch[0] but keep bevfinal as the canvas/clamp target, seamcore mask. Gate+vision both. Sweep donor in {virtual-centre stitch, neighbor-cam slab} x shift in {0,1,2 latent cols}.
directions.gpu_cost_est: ~2 A100-hr. Sub-test B needs a 2nd invert (donor) but that is one-time; reverse passes are cheap. Note FLUX latent is 16x downsampled so shift granularity is ~16px ERP blocks — fine for the wavy seam, not hairline.
directions.kill_criteria: If hard token-replacement creates a NEW mini-seam at the donor/target boundary that the halo cannot hide, AND the additive fallback (Direction 7) also fails -> kill. If the donor stitch's own geometry conflicts with bevfinal causing ghosting -> kill (the very failure single-source was meant to avoid).
directions.expected_payoff: Medium-high. The conditioning lens's strongest claim: the entire shift_mask/donor machinery is built but never used; this is the only lever that gives the seam REAL pixels to copy instead of inventing. Highest novelty.
directions.novelty_note: Done-list v18 'reference canvas' fed L1 camera evidence as the GENERATION target/canvas and asked DiT to fill missing cameras (cooperative stitcher) — NEG. This is the opposite wiring: real evidence is the read-only DONOR (batch[0] token source / shift_mask), bevfinal stays the canvas. Self-reference donor (current) and evidence-as-canvas (v18) are both explored; evidence-as-donor is not.

directions.name: Sky-outpaint generalization + per-encoder anti-object prompt hardening

directions.name: RF gamma x eta-decay faithfulness micro-sweep
directions.summary: gamma (inversion fidelity, invert line 315 hardcoded 1.0) and decay_eta/eta_decay_power (never enabled) are the continuous faithfulness dials that the binary tau token-replace approximates discretely. A too-rigid gamma=1.0 inversion can make the latent reconstruct the source so exactly the model resists ANY edit — one root cause of the thin-seam no-op. Lowering gamma slightly gives edit-room from a still-source-consistent start; eta_decay relaxes the anchor only in late steps so outpaint gains detail without early drift. Cheap because the source is inverted once per gamma.

T1: on the v14 thin r008/tau8 config, sweep gamma in {0.6, 0.8, 1.0}; pick the gamma where core MAE rises off the no-op floor while far MAE stays ~3. T2: on opmask_sky, keep gamma=1.0 on content, enable decay_eta=True, sweep eta_decay_power in {1,2}; check the outpainted sky gains gradient detail without the FoV content drifting. Gate+vision every output. Each gamma value = 1 extra invert; eta_decay is reverse-only (free).
directions.gpu_cost_est: ~2 A100-hr: 3 inverts (gamma) + ~6 reverse passes across both targets, single load.
directions.kill_criteria: If lowering gamma to 0.6 still under-changes the seam (no-op) OR starts drifting far-region pixels (far MAE climbs) -> gamma is not the unlock, drop. If decay_eta produces no visible sky-detail gain -> drop, keep eta=1 fixed.
directions.expected_payoff: Low-medium. A finer faithfulness dial than tau; most useful as a knob to COMBINE with Direction 1 (low gamma + short window). Marginal alone.
directions.novelty_note: Done-list swept tau/steps/seed/guidance but explicitly NOT gamma (invert always gamma=1.0) and NEVER decay_eta. These are distinct RF-Inversion knobs untouched by any prior run.

directions.name: PersonalizeAnything layer-subset injection (set_attn_module_names)

Deep/double-stream blocks carry structure (lane lines, curb geometry); shallow/single blocks carry texture. Inject source tokens ONLY in deep blocks to hold geometry byte-faithful while shallow layers freely repaint seam TEXTURE -> directly attacks no-op-vs-melt from a structurally orthogonal axis. For T2 sky, the inverse (shallow-only) makes generated sky inherit source exposure/color while deep layers invent plausible sky gradient. Entirely unswept axis.

T2-sky: shallow-texture subset on opmask_sky. Gate+vision each. First confirm which block-name prefixes exist via list(pipe.transformer.attn_processors.keys()) and split by structure/texture depth.

directions.novelty_note: Done-list never touched layer placement — every prior run injected PA into ALL attn layers. set_attn_module_names is a built-but-unused argument; this is a new control surface, not a re-parameterization of mask/tau.

directions.name: Cube-face-space objective seam metric + targeted polar-face QA gate
directions.summary: Adds an OBJECTIVE selection/QA metric that none of the prior runs had — the wavy near-ground seam is an ERP curve but becomes a near-STRAIGHT step defect on the -Y (down/ground) cube face, far easier to score than ERP edge energy. Use cube_map_from_equirectangular as (a) the per-region objective driving the multi-yaw SELECT in Direction 2, and (b) a polar-face QA gate for T2: after sky/ground outpaint, convert to cube and inspect +Y/-Y faces for hallucinated polar structure; if a face shows invented geometry, mask just that face region back to flat and re-run. This is QA/scoring substrate, not a generation change, so it adds faithfulness SAFETY rather than risk.
directions.how_to_test: Reuse external/DiT360/src/cube_map.cube_map_from_equirectangular (ERP->6 faces, grid_sample). For T1: for each multi-yaw candidate (Direction 2), cube-project, measure Sobel edge energy on the down(-Y) face in the seam band, feed as the argmin objective instead of raw ERP gradient. For T2: cube-project the sky-outpaint winner, eyeball +Y face; if clean, accept. Use py360convert for the inverse cube->ERP round-trip if a face needs local re-mask. No new generation params; pure measurement loop wrapped around Directions 2 and 4.
directions.gpu_cost_est: Near-zero GPU (cube ops are grid_sample on CPU/GPU, seconds). Cost is only the underlying generation it scores.
directions.kill_criteria: If down-face edge energy does NOT correlate with the visually-judged seam quality (metric disagrees with vision) -> fall back to vision-only selection, drop the metric. Per project rule, vision wins on conflict.
directions.expected_payoff: Low-medium standalone, but multiplies the value of Direction 2 by giving it a principled objective. Mainly a force-multiplier + an extra T2 safety gate.
directions.novelty_note: Done-list judged everything with the torchvision OBJECT gate + ERP vision; it NEVER used cube-face-space as a seam metric or a polar-face QA gate. cube_map is a training-side op never invoked at inference here.

directions.name: Additive concept_process conditioning (soft K/V append) as the blend-friendly donor mode
directions.summary: The fallback/companion to Direction 3. Where hard token-replacement (shift_mask) creates a new paste boundary, set concept_process=True so the real neighbor-cam / LiDAR-ground tokens are APPENDED as extra attendable keys/values (IP-Adapter-style) with their original rotary positions, rather than overwriting target latents. FLUX then ATTENDS to the real evidence as context while denoising the region freely -> softer, blend-friendly pull toward real color/texture/structure with no hard cut. Stays gate-clean because the appended reference is real evidence and the region is still constrained by the clamp + object gate.
directions.how_to_test: PersonalizeAnythingAttnProcessor already has concept_process flag + get_concept_rotary_emb (built, default False). In the runner lambda set concept_process=True and feed the real neighbor-cam crop (T1 halo zone) or a real sky strip (T2 tone-match) as the donor. Keep guidance low (~2.8) so the appended reference dominates the text prior. Run ONLY if Direction 3's hard shift_mask shows a paste-edge artifact. Gate+vision; compare paste-edge sharpness vs Direction 3.
directions.gpu_cost_est: ~1 A100-hr incremental on top of Direction 3 (same donor invert, reverse-only, slightly more tokens in attn).
directions.kill_criteria: If additive conditioning is too weak to pull the seam toward the evidence (under-changes, like the no-op floor) OR if appended tokens destabilize the wrap -> drop. Strictly a tie-breaker for Direction 3.
directions.expected_payoff: Low. Conditional on Direction 3 needing a softer boundary; not worth running independently.
directions.novelty_note: concept_process (additive K/V append) has never been enabled in any prior run — all runs used hard token-replacement or pixel/latent compose. This is the built-but-unused additive branch of the SAME processor, distinct from the replacement-mode and from post-compose blending.

levers.name: RF-Inversion editing window (start_timestep / stop_timestep)
levers.paper_basis: pa_src/pipeline.py __call__ args start_timestep/stop_timestep -> mapped to integer step indices (lines 966-973); eta is applied ONLY for start<=i<stop (line 1032 `eta_t = eta if start_timestep <= i < stop_timestep else 0.0`). The RF-Inversion paper (2410.10792 Alg.2) defines this as the interval over which the source-anchoring vector field v_t_cond pulls latents toward the inverted image.
levers.how_to_exploit: Our runner hardcodes start_timestep=0.0, stop_timestep=0.99 (so eta=1 anchors over the WHOLE loop -> maximal faithfulness everywhere, leaving generation to come only from the seam/outpaint mask). This is the single biggest UNUSED knob. T1-seam: set start_timestep=0.0, stop_timestep~0.3-0.5 so the model is anchored to source early and only does mild texture editing in the seam zone in late steps -> hides the wavy seam WITHOUT the late-step free-running that currently invents cars. T2-outpaint: opposite — stop_timestep high (0.8-0.99) keeps content anchored while the masked-black sky/ground band (which has no source to anchor to) is free to fill the full loop; sweep stop_timestep down to find the point where outpaint stays continuous but content stops drifting.

levers.name: eta strength + eta decay (eta / decay_eta / eta_decay_power)
levers.paper_basis: pipeline.py __call__ eta=1.0 default, plus decay_eta (bool) and eta_decay_power (float) at lines 742-743, applied at lines 1033-1037 `eta_t = eta_t * (1 - i/num_inference_steps)**eta_decay_power`. Docstring (lines 786-788): 'higher eta -> better faithfulness, less editability'.
levers.how_to_exploit: Our runner passes eta=1.0 fixed and never sets decay_eta. eta is the continuous faithfulness dial that PersonalizeAnything-tau does discretely. T1-seam: lower eta to ~0.7-0.85 ONLY enough to let the seam ribbon re-texture while the rest stays locked — gives a smoother faithfulness/editability tradeoff than the binary tau token-replace. T2-outpaint: keep eta=1 on content but enable decay_eta with eta_decay_power~1-2 so the anchor relaxes in late steps and the generated sky/ground gains detail/diversity without early-step drift. Sweep eta in {0.7,0.85,1.0} x decay_eta {off,on} — never done.

levers.name: Inversion gamma (forward controlled ODE)
levers.paper_basis: pipe.invert(gamma=...) at pipeline.py line 1117, used at line 1267 `u_hat = u_t + gamma*(u_t_cond - u_t)` (Eq.8). Higher gamma -> the inverted noise stays closer to a reconstructable trajectory of the SOURCE image. Our runner calls invert(..., gamma=1.0) at run_dit360_trimap_clamp.py line 315.
levers.how_to_exploit: gamma=1.0 is the strongest-faithfulness inversion; never varied. Because we invert the source ONCE for all cases, gamma is essentially free to sweep (one extra invert per value). T1-seam & T2-outpaint both: a too-high gamma can make the inverted latent rigidly reconstruct the source so the model resists ANY edit (one cause of seam no-op at low tau). Try gamma in {0.5, 0.7, 1.0}: lower gamma gives the reverse pass more freedom to smooth the seam / blend the outpaint boundary while still starting from a source-consistent point. Pair a slightly lower gamma with a short stop_timestep to get edit-room without hallucination.

levers.name: PersonalizeAnything injection LAYER subset (set_attn_module_names)
levers.paper_basis: pa_src/attn_processor.py set_flux_transformer_attn_processor takes set_attn_module_names (prefix-match list, lines 18-24); our runner installs the PA processor on EVERY attn layer (lambda over all names, run_dit360_trimap_clamp.py lines 366-375) so token-replacement happens in all double+single Flux blocks. PA paper injects reference tokens to anchor identity; which blocks carry structure vs texture differs by depth.
levers.how_to_exploit: We inject into ALL blocks uniformly — never subsetted. Pass set_attn_module_names to restrict token-replacement to e.g. only the double-stream blocks (transformer_blocks.*) or only late single blocks. T1-seam: inject the source tokens only in deep/structure layers so geometry (lane lines, curb) is held byte-faithful while shallow texture layers are free to repaint the seam smoothly — directly attacks the 'no-op vs melt' dichotomy. T2-outpaint: the inverse — inject in shallow texture layers so the generated sky inherits source color/exposure statistics while deep layers freely invent plausible sky geometry. This is an entirely unswept axis of PA.

levers.name: PersonalizeAnything tau as a TIMESTEP gate (which steps replace tokens)
levers.paper_basis: attn_processor.py line 76 `t_flag = timestep > self.tau` gates token replacement (r_q/r_k/r_v) — replacement happens only while normalized timestep > tau/100, i.e. the EARLY (high-noise) steps. tau is the boundary. Our runner sets tau in {5,20,50}.
levers.how_to_exploit: tau magnitude was swept (findings: 5=no-op, 20-50=melt for seam) but tau is really a STEP-WINDOW knob, and it interacts with start/stop_timestep which we never co-varied. T1-seam: keep tau moderate but COMBINE with a short RF stop_timestep so early steps replace source tokens (lock structure) and the un-anchored late steps only do gentle denoise -> seam blends without late-step object invention. T2-outpaint: a LOW tau (replace tokens for almost all steps) over the PRESERVE region keeps content pinned while the masked band generates — current sky-outpaint win used tau=50; try tau=10-20 to pin content harder and see if sky boundary continuity improves. Sweep tau x stop_timestep jointly (2D), which has never been done.

levers.name: Sampling steps + custom sigma/timestep schedule (num_inference_steps / sigmas / timesteps)
levers.paper_basis: pipeline.py accepts num_inference_steps (default 28), and custom `sigmas` / `timesteps` lists via retrieve_timesteps (lines 940-965, 748-749). Default sigmas = np.linspace(1.0, 1/N, N) (line 942). Our runner uses steps=50 and never passes custom sigmas. invert uses the SAME N as reverse.
levers.how_to_exploit: Step count was bumped 28->50 but the sigma SPACING is still uniform-linear and never customized. T1-seam: feed a custom `sigmas` schedule that is dense in the LATE (low-noise) steps where seam micro-texture is decided, so the seam repaint is high-quality without adding early free-generation steps. T2-outpaint: dense EARLY sigmas help the large masked band acquire coherent global structure (sky gradient) before detail. Also note inversion N must match reverse N — sweeping steps changes both; an under-explored cheap lever (FID/continuity vs steps curve never measured here).

levers.name: Circular-padding width / wrap latent seam (the 1-column ERP wrap)
levers.paper_basis: DiT360's core token-level module is position-aware circular padding for 0/360 continuity (paper sec 3.3). In code it is realized as a ONE-column latent wrap applied consistently in invert (pipeline.py 1179-1189), reverse-latent prep (919-924), mask (run_dit360_trimap_clamp.py line 343 `torch.cat([mask[:,0:1],mask,mask[:,-1:]])`), latent weights (_latent_weights wrap, lines 136-138) and stripped at the end (1083-1085). Fixed width = 1 latent col.
levers.how_to_exploit: We inherit the 1-col wrap (good — it is why the 0/360 ERP seam stays continuous) but it is FIXED at 1 column and only at the image's left/right wrap, NOT at our INTERNAL near-ground seam. T1-seam: the internal wavy seam is NOT a circular boundary, so circular padding does nothing for it — exploit instead by re-using the same wrap mechanism to give the seam-mask a symmetric few-pixel latent halo so PA token-replacement blends across the cut (we already dilate in pixel space via halo_px; consider doing it in LATENT space to match the wrap). T2-outpaint: confirm the wrap keeps the outpainted sky continuous across 0/360 (it does) — keep as-is; widening to 2 cols is a cheap robustness try for the left/right outpaint seam.

levers.name: Dual text encoders + per-branch prompt (prompt vs prompt_2, parallel batch[0]/batch[1])
levers.paper_basis: pipeline runs a PARALLEL batch of 2 (source-anchored slot [0], edited slot [1]); __call__ takes prompt AND prompt_2 (T5 vs CLIP, lines 734-735) and our runner passes the SAME prompt twice ([args.prompt, args.prompt], run line 378). FLUX.1-dev is guidance-distilled (guidance_embeds true, lines 980-984) so guidance_scale is an embedded scalar, NOT true CFG — there is no negative-prompt branch.
levers.how_to_exploit: We use one positive prompt, duplicated, and never touch prompt_2. T2-outpaint: set a sky-only descriptive prompt ('clear continuous overcast sky, no objects') for the generated band; use prompt_2 (CLIP pooled) vs prompt (T5) asymmetrically to push global style on one encoder and local texture on the other. Since FLUX-dev has no CFG negative, prompt wording is the ONLY semantic steering — currently un-tuned per target.

For T2: when outpainting the sky/ground band, trust the wrap so the left/right edges of the band stay continuous; just ensure any mask we pass is column-wrapped exactly like editing.py:44 or it desyncs from the padded latent.

levers.name: Yaw-loss rotation robustness -> multi-yaw generate-and-SELECT
levers.paper_basis: src/dit360.py 213-225 trains loss_yaw using src/yaw_rotate.equirectangular_rotate_yaw (true spherical yaw remap via 3D rotation matrix, NOT a pixel roll). The LoRA is thus trained to be yaw-equivariant, so the same scene at different yaw offsets is near-equally plausible but per-region artifacts land at different azimuths each pass.
levers.how_to_exploit: T1 primary (helps T2). Pick N yaw offsets (e.g. 0/45/.../315 deg). For each: spherically yaw-rotate the bevfinal base with equirectangular_rotate_yaw (reuse src/yaw_rotate.py verbatim), run the SAME thin-seam-mask seam-hide edit, then yaw-rotate the result BACK by -offset to re-register. Stack the N re-registered panos and SELECT per-region the cleanest pixels along the seam band (min local-gradient / min cube-face edge energy, see cube lever), NEVER average (averaging reblurs — matches the project's confirmed single-source>averaging finding). Each pass puts the residual near-ground wave at a different phase, so per-region min-artifact selection collapses it. Cheap pilot: 3 offsets first to confirm artifacts decorrelate before committing to 8.

levers.name: Cube-loss distortion awareness -> verify/repair in cube-face space
levers.paper_basis: src/dit360.py 227-236 trains loss_cube using src/cube_map.cube_map_from_equirectangular (grid_sample ERP->6 faces: lateral front/right/back/left + up/down). cube_map.py is a standalone reusable ERP->cube op; the LoRA is trained so face-wise structure (esp. polar) is coherent.
levers.how_to_exploit: T1 verify + T2 generate. The near-ground wavy seam is an ERP curve but becomes a FLAT structure on the -Y (down/ground) cube face where waviness is a straight-line step defect, far easier to detect/score. T1: run cube_map_from_equirectangular on each seam-hide candidate, measure edge energy on the down face / lateral face the seam crosses, and use THAT as the objective selection metric driving the multi-yaw select. T2: after sky/ground outpaint, convert to cube and inspect +Y (sky) / -Y (ground) faces for the polar smear the cube-loss prior is meant to suppress; if a face shows hallucinated structure, mask just that face region back to flat and re-run. Use py360convert (README-recommended) for the inverse cube->ERP round-trip. Cube faces are the QA gate, not the generation substrate — keeps us source-faithful.

levers.name: Perspective-image-guidance realism prior on a masked ERP band
levers.paper_basis: Paper 3.2 + README mix-training: LoRA trained on 40k real perspective photos projected as cubemap lateral faces into masked ERP regions, supervised ONLY inside mask M (L_perspective = MSE(eps*M, eps_hat*M)). So the LoRA learned to paint photoreal texture/lighting inside a masked ERP sub-region from real-photo statistics, NOT to invent global geometry (sec 12 / ablation: it is the realism teacher, not the geometry teacher).
levers.how_to_exploit: T1 primary. Our seam content IS real ring-cam perspective imagery — exactly the lateral-face-photo-in-ERP-region domain this branch was trained to make photoreal. Scope the seam-hide edit to a THIN masked ERP band over the seam and let the LoRA re-render only texture/lighting continuity there; because the branch teaches texture/light/detail and explicitly NOT geometry, it closes the seam WITHOUT inventing salient objects. This is the code-level reason thin seam-TEXTURE closure is faithfulness-safe while large seam-COMPLETION holes invent cars (memory NEG). Keep the mask in the mid-latitude lateral band where this prior is strongest.

levers.name: RF-Inversion gamma + eta/[start,stop] denoise window = faithfulness dial
levers.paper_basis: pa_src/pipeline.py invert() applies gamma (u_hat = u_t + gamma*(u_cond - u_t), line ~1267); generation injects controlled noise eta ONLY inside start_timestep<=i<stop_timestep (line ~1032: eta_t = eta if window else 0.0). editing.py uses gamma=1.0, start=0.0, stop=0.99, eta=1.0.
levers.how_to_exploit: Both targets. gamma sets how hard inversion is pulled toward the source; eta+[start,stop] set WHERE in denoising the model may deviate from the inverted source trajectory. T1 seam-hide wants minimal deviation: SHRINK the window (start=0.0, stop~0.2-0.3 instead of 0.99) so the model only nudges early-step structure at the seam then snaps back to source, preserving non-seam pixels near-exactly. T2 outpaint needs more freedom in the black band but constraint elsewhere: keep a wider window and rely on the preserve-mask (mask=1 keeps source) so only the out-of-FoV region is synthesized. Sweep stop_timestep as the single knob trading faithfulness vs seam-smoothing; pick the winner via the cube-face edge metric (cube lever) + the torchvision object gate.

levers.name: PersonalizeAnything tau token-replacement gate = source anchoring
levers.paper_basis: pa_src/attn_processor.py: t_flag = timestep > tau forces masked-region q/k/v to the SOURCE (concept) features hidden_states[mask] during early (high-timestep) steps while preserving positional encodings; mask=1 = preserved source. tau in 0..1 (editing.py tau=50/100); smaller tau = stronger source consistency per the editing.py comment.
levers.how_to_exploit: Both targets — the core faithfulness lever; memory's working default is tau=50. Mechanism: at early steps the model is FORCED to use source tokens inside the preserved mask, hard-anchoring everything outside the thin seam strip (T1) or outside the black band (T2) to bevfinal — this is what keeps net-new salient objects out and passes the object gate. T1: preserved=1 everywhere EXCEPT the thin seam strip (the strip is where generation is allowed); lower tau toward 30-40 if off-seam drift appears, raise toward 50-60 if the strip looks too locked to hide the seam. T2: preserved=1 over the real FoV, =0 over sky/ground band, tau~50 so FoV is pinned and only the band is synthesized. Always set mask per README (mask = 1-mask for inpainting holes) and column-wrap it (editing.py:44) to align with the circular-padded latent.

levers.name: Lateral-face-only training bias -> split T2 into sky vs ground passes by latitude
levers.paper_basis: Paper 3.2 + 02 notes: perspective branch restricted to cubemap LATERAL faces (sky/ground = rare angles, excluded); panoramic refinement (Fig 3) instead INPAINTS the blurry top/bottom faces of Matterport3D before training. So the LoRA's photoreal prior is strong on the equatorial band but its polar prior is a refinement/inpainting prior, not a photo-realism one.
levers.how_to_exploit: Splits our targets by latitude. T1 near-ground seam sits just below the equator — keep its mask in the lateral band, do NOT push it into polar rows. T2 splits into two sub-problems matching two trained priors: (a) SKY band (upper pole) -> exploit the panoramic-refinement/inpainting prior (gate-clean fill = the confirmed WIN in memory); constraint + object-gate sky pass with prompt like 'clear sky'. (b) GROUND band (lower pole) -> same refinement prior but weaker texture (model never saw photoreal downward views); hard-constrain to flat ground color/gradient, prompt 'road ground plane', and gate with the cube down-face check (cube lever). Run sky and ground as SEPARATE masked passes with different prompts, not one polar outpaint, because the trained prior treats them as distinct refinement targets.

levers.name: 1024x2048 native-resolution lock
levers.paper_basis: README inference note: trained only at 1024x2048, other sizes -> abnormal results; inference.py/editing.py hardcode height=1024 width=2048; circular-pad math assumes n_h=H/16, n_w=W/16; ~37GB VRAM unoptimized.
levers.how_to_exploit: Both targets, guardrail. Our base is SR_bmw_bevfinal_1024x2048 so we are on-spec — keep every generative pass at exactly 1024x2048 or the yaw/cube/circular priors (all tied to the latent grid math) degrade. If a higher-res deliverable is needed, do the DiT360 edit at 1024x2048 then SR the RESULT; never feed off-size ERP into the pipeline. Budget the multi-yaw select loop (yaw lever) as SEQUENTIAL single-image passes (~37GB each), not a batch, to fit GPU. This lever mainly defines what NOT to vary so the other levers stay valid.

lens_reads.notes:
All 8 levers are grounded in the actual DiT360 code under external/DiT360, not just paper prose. Load-bearing files: external/DiT360/src/pipeline.py (837-853, 980-984 = inference-time circular padding done FOR us), external/DiT360/src/dit360.py (213-250 = yaw+cube training losses, expose reusable ops), external/DiT360/src/yaw_rotate.py (equirectangular_rotate_yaw, reuse verbatim for multi-yaw select), external/DiT360/src/cube_map.py (cube_map_from_equirectangular, reuse as seam-QA metric + polar-face check), external/DiT360/editing.py (RF-Inversion + PersonalizeAnything wiring, tau=50, gamma=1.0, mask wrap line 44), external/DiT360/pa_src/attn_processor.py (tau gate t_flag=timestep>tau), external/DiT360/pa_src/pipeline.py (invert gamma ~1267, eta window ~1032).

Strongest NEW levers (already_used=no) to act on: (2) multi-yaw generate-and-SELECT for T1 — weaponizes the yaw-robustness prior AND the project's confirmed single-source>averaging finding; and (3) cube-face-space VERIFY giving an OBJECTIVE seam metric (the ERP seam curve flattens into a straight-line step defect on the -Y down face). These COMPOSE into one loop: yaw-rotate -> thin-seam-hide -> rotate back -> score in cube-face space -> select per-region min-edge-energy. Circular padding (lever 1) lets us also ROLL a stubborn seam to the benign 0/360 azimuth.

Reconciling with MEMORY: memory says sky-only OUTPAINT is the WIN and seam-COMPLETION is NEG (invents cars). Levers 4 + 7 explain WHY at code level — the perspective-guidance realism prior is texture-only on lateral faces, so thin seam-TEXTURE closure (T1) is faithfulness-safe whereas large seam holes trigger object hallucination; and ground outpaint is weaker than sky because the model never trained on photoreal downward views, so ground must be hard-constrained + cube-down-face gated. tau (lever 6) + the eta/gamma window (lever 5) are the two faithfulness dials that keep both targets passing the torchvision object gate; for T1 specifically, shrink stop_timestep (~0.2-0.3) instead of the editing.py default 0.99 to minimize off-seam drift.

Caveats: yaw-loss and cube-loss are TRAINING losses — we cannot toggle them at inference, only exploit the resulting robustness indirectly (the LoRA is already yaw/cube robust). The multi-yaw select assumes per-pass artifacts decorrelate across offsets; run a 3-offset pilot before 8. Every generative output still must pass the existing torchvision object gate + vision regardless of lever, per the project's hard faithfulness constraint.

levers.name: Decoupled shift_mask: relocate REAL neighbor-cam tokens across the seam
levers.paper_basis: external/DiT360/pa_src/attn_processor.py PersonalizeAnythingAttnProcessor.__init__(self, name, mask, device, tau, shift_mask=None,...): reference tokens are READ from batch[0] at `self.mask` positions (concept_feature_ = hidden_states[0, mask]) and WRITTEN into batch[1] at `self.shift_mask` positions (image_hidden_states[shift_mask]=concept_feature_). shift_mask defaults to mask (pure self-reference) but is an independent argument. The utils.shift_tensor helper exists for exactly this.
levers.how_to_exploit: T1 seam-hide: build TWO masks. `mask` (donor) = a strip of the OPPOSITE side of the seam that shows the same physical surface captured cleanly by the neighbor camera (e.g. the lane/curb pixels a few px left of the seam that the left cam saw well). `shift_mask` (target) = the wavy/ghosted seam strip to be repaired, shifted by the disparity (a few latent columns). Pass shift_mask into PersonalizeAnythingAttnProcessor so FLUX paints the seam using the REAL neighbor-cam appearance instead of inventing texture. Keep tau low (5-15) so token replacement dominates early steps. This turns the attn-processor from a copy-self into a copy-real-neighbor rein, bounding hallucination to evidence that actually exists in an adjacent camera.

levers.name: Swap the donor: invert a REAL evidence image into batch[0] instead of the panorama itself
levers.paper_basis: external/DiT360/editing.py + pa_src/pipeline.py __call__: the pipeline runs batch of 2; batch[0] is the source reconstruction produced by pipe.invert(image=init_image) and acts as the token donor, batch[1] is the edited output. Nothing requires the donor and the canvas to be the same image — invert() takes any PipelineImageInput, and the in-loop consistency line `latents[1]=latents[1]*(1-mask)+latents[0]*mask` plus the attn donor both read batch[0].
levers.how_to_exploit: T2 ground outpaint: render the missing ground band from LiDAR (BEV-projected road/intensity) or paste the real overlapping-cam ground, ERP-warp it into a full 2048x1024 canvas, and invert THAT as batch[0]; keep our faithful bevfinal as batch[1]. Set the outpaint generate-mask (from _outpaint_mask.py `ground`/`band`) so DiT360 only fills the band, but now the donor latents it pulls from are real LiDAR ground, not Flux's imagination -> faithful road continuation, no invented crosswalks/cars. Same trick for T1: donor = an alternative clean stitch (e.g. virtual-centre single-source) so the seam repair copies real geometry.

levers.name: concept_process token-concatenation (IP-Adapter-style cross-image K/V append)
levers.paper_basis: external/DiT360/pa_src/attn_processor.py: c_q/c_kv branch (concept_process flag, default False). When enabled it does c_key=attn.to_k(concept_feature_); key=torch.cat([key,c_key]) and gives the appended tokens their ORIGINAL rotary positions via get_concept_rotary_emb. This ADDS reference tokens as extra attendable keys/values rather than overwriting target latents.
levers.how_to_exploit: Where hard token-replacement (shift_mask) causes seams/discontinuities, instead set concept_process=True and feed the real neighbor-cam crop (or LiDAR ground) as concept_feature_. FLUX then ATTENDS to the real evidence as additional context while still denoising the target region freely -> softer, blend-friendly conditioning that pulls color/texture/structure toward the evidence without a hard paste boundary. Good for T1 halo zone (the yellow band in run_dit360_trimap_clamp) and for T2 sky tone-matching. Combine with low guidance (~2.8) so the appended reference dominates over the text prior.

levers.name: MultiPersonalizeAnythingAttnProcessor: multiple real-evidence donors at once
levers.paper_basis: external/DiT360/pa_src/attn_processor.py MultiPersonalizeAnythingAttnProcessor(masks=[...], shift_masks=[...]): loops over a LIST of (mask, shift_mask) pairs, each extracting its own concept_feature_ and writing to its own shift target; rotary emb concatenates all donor masks. Built but never wired into editing.py or our runner.
levers.how_to_exploit: T1 has up to 6 seams (7 cams). Provide one (mask,shift_mask) pair per seam so each seam is repaired from its OWN correct neighbor camera in a single forward pass, instead of one global self-reference. For T2, use multiple donors for the ground band: one mask=LiDAR-road donor for the lower band, one mask=real-sky-strip donor for the upper band, each relocated to its target region. This scales the neighbor-evidence rein to the whole panorama and keeps every fill anchored to the physically-correct source.

levers.name: Perspective-Image-Guidance mix-training on OUR real cams (LoRA fine-tune, faithful domain)
levers.paper_basis: external/DiT360/README.md Mix Training + src/dynamic_dataset.py preprocess_mixed_stage_train + src/dit360_mix_staged.py cube2pano branch: perspective images enter as {image, caption, mask}, projected to ERP via py360convert, and loss is computed ONLY inside the valid-projection mask (all_masked_losses). This is exactly the 'real photo -> ERP region -> masked supervision' recipe, and the masked-loss path is generic to ANY masked ERP region.
levers.how_to_exploit: We already HAVE faithful per-camera ERP slabs + their valid masks (the bevfinal build produces them). Build a small jsonl of our 7 AV2 cams as the 'perspective' branch and our best stitched panos as the 'panorama' branch, then LoRA-finetune DiT360 a few hundred steps. This teaches the model OUR sensor's road/sky/building statistics so that at T1/T2 inference its prior already matches our domain (no NuScenes/landscape look, far less tendency to invent salient objects). The masked-loss path also lets us supervise ONLY the seam/band regions, i.e. a region-specialised seam-repair LoRA.

levers.name: Cube-loss consistency as an inference-time structure rein (cube_map_from_equirectangular)
levers.paper_basis: external/DiT360/src/cube_map.py cube_map_from_equirectangular + dit360_mix_staged.py loss_cube: ERP is projected to 6 perspective cube faces; supervision on the faces enforces undistorted, perspective-correct structure especially near poles/ground. Purely training-side today.
levers.how_to_exploit: Add a per-step callback (we already use callback_on_step_end in run_dit360_trimap_clamp.py) that decodes the current ground/seam region, cube-projects it, and nudges latents toward cube-face consistency with the REAL evidence (neighbor-cam cube face or LiDAR cube face). For T2 ground especially, the down (-Y) cube face is where ERP smears road into curved garbage; constraining that face to the LiDAR/BEV road keeps lane lines straight and stops invented road furniture. Cheap, training-free, and directly attacks the 'wavy near-ground seam' physical floor noted in memory.

levers.name: RoPE position-id offset for reference tokens (_prepare_latent_image_ids_offset)
levers.paper_basis: external/DiT360/pa_src/pipeline.py _prepare_latent_image_ids_offset(..., x_offset=0, y_offset=32) and the circular-padding wrap in invert()/__call__ (last_col/first_col concat). Position ids are explicit and editable; the attn processor's get_concept_rotary_emb already reassigns rotary positions to relocated reference tokens.
levers.how_to_exploit: When relocating neighbor-cam tokens across a seam (lever 1) or extending the ground band (lever 2), the donor pixels come from a slightly different yaw/pitch. Give the relocated reference tokens position-ids matching their TARGET panoramic location (and the correct parallax-shifted column) via the offset helper, so RoPE tells FLUX 'this evidence belongs HERE'. This makes the relocated real evidence blend geometrically instead of appearing as a misplaced patch, and exploits the existing circular-padding columns so the wrap-around 0/360 seam is also covered.

levers.name: Anti-hallucination prompt + Cube-Composer coverage/future-fragment context
levers.paper_basis: Our DEFAULT_PROMPT in run_dit360_trimap_clamp.py literally enumerates 'cars, lane markings, signs, buildings' (invites salient objects). DiT360 outpaint is text-conditioned (pipeline encode_prompt). Cube Composer (paper_reading/02_Cube Composer.md sec 6-8) adds the 'context mechanism': coverage-guided order (generate the most-observed region first) and future-fragment tokens (use frames where the camera LATER saw the region as real evidence).
levers.how_to_exploit: T1/T2 prompt: drop the object list; use 'continue the existing road, sky and building surfaces; smooth seam; invent no new vehicles, people, signs or objects; empty scene'. This biases the text prior away from net-new salient objects (which our torchvision object-gate rejects anyway -> fewer wasted gens). Borrow Cube-Composer's reins without its model: (a) coverage order — fill the seam/band region that has the MOST adjacent real evidence first, then condition later regions on it; (b) future-fragment — for AV2 we have neighboring TIMESTAMPS where a camera panned over the now-occluded ground/seam; warp that real frame in as the donor (lever 2) so even 'unseen at t' regions are filled from real pixels seen at t±k, not hallucinated.

lens_reads.notes:
Strongest under-exploited lever by far is the donor/shift_mask split inside PersonalizeAnythingAttnProcessor (levers 1-4): the code already supports reading reference tokens from one place/image and writing them somewhere else, and running a 2-element batch where batch[0] is an arbitrary inverted donor image. Today editing.py and our run_dit360_trimap_clamp.py only use SELF-reference (shift_mask=mask, donor=the same panorama), so DiT360 is currently a self-consistency clamp, NOT an evidence rein. Pointing the donor at real neighbor-cam pixels or LiDAR-rendered ground converts it into exactly the 'real evidence bounds hallucination' mechanism the project wants — and it is training-free (just new mask construction + a second invert()). 

Caveats: (1) FLUX VAE latent is 16x downsampled and packed, so a 'few-px parallax shift' across the seam is sub-latent-pixel; relocation works at the granularity of ~16px ERP blocks, fine for the wavy seam/ground band but not for hairline alignment. (2) Hard token-replacement (shift_mask) can itself create a new mini-seam at the donor/target boundary — that's what the halo zone + concept_process (additive, lever 3) is for; prefer additive conditioning when a hard paste edge appears. (3) Memory says learned single-centre stitching tested WORSE and seam-completion DiT360 INVENTS cars; both are consistent with the model running in self/text-prior mode — the fix here (real-evidence donor + anti-object prompt + object-gate) is the untested variant, not a re-run of the negative. (4) The mix-training LoRA (lever 5) needs GPU + a few hundred steps but is the only lever that fixes the DOMAIN prior (NuScenes/landscape look) at the root; everything else is inference-time. (5) DiT360 ships NO ControlNet; structure conditioning (edges/lines/depth) would require an external FLUX.1-dev ControlNet — viable but out-of-repo, so I encoded the in-repo structure rein as cube-loss consistency (lever 6) instead. I verified every claim against the actual source files (attn_processor.py, pipeline.py, editing.py, cube_map.py, dit360_mix_staged.py, dynamic_dataset.py, run_dit360_trimap_clamp.py, _outpaint_mask.py); the self_learning/DiT 360.md note is empty (1 line).
